(medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/ · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://enterprisearchitecture.harvard.edu/user-research-methods-and-recommendations
- [statement] For each research round, plan participant inclusion and access needs, recruitment budget, informed consent, recording or note-taking responsibilities, and time for analysis. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-round-of-user-research · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research strategy and method selection
- [statement] Plan how findings will enter team decisions and where outputs will be stored and shared. Research scheduling should stay aligned with the team’s priorities and ability to act on findings. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/plan-user-research-for-your-service · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research strategy and method selection
- [statement] Triangulation combines multiple sources or approaches to examine a question from different viewpoints. It can use complementary qualitative and quantitative evidence, existing records, or separate researcher analyses; it does not require a fixed number of methods. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/triangulation-better-research-results-using-multiple-ux-methods/ · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research strategy and method selection · also: https://dscout.com/people-nerds/triangulate-user-research
- [statement] NN/g’s 2024 guidance recommends treating synthetic-user outputs as hypotheses to test with real people, and explicitly identifying their origin. They should not be presented as findings from human participants or used to replace real-user research. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/synthetic-users/ · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research strategy and method selection
- [statement] Keep observation, interpretation and action distinct: record what participants said or did, group similar observations into themes, write findings for the groups, and attach proposed actions. Coding and grouping help connect raw evidence to recommendations. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/analyse-a-research-session · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://dscout.com/people-nerds/user-research-synthesis
- [statement] GOV.UK recommends grouping observations into themes, splitting overly broad groups, and attaching findings and proposed actions to their relevant groups so the reasoning remains connected to the observations. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/analyse-a-research-session · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] Klement proposes identifying a high-level job and smaller contributing jobs, observing the current solution, formulating Job Stories around causality, motivations and anxieties, then creating a feature or interface solution. His article illustrates this workflow with one team’s profile-page design. (low confidence) — https://www.intercom.com/blog/using-job-stories-design-features-ui-ux · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] The persona-visualization study reports that presentation influenced persona perception and could somewhat reduce stereotyping; its sample consisted of computer-science students, so the finding does not establish that personas eliminate bias across professional design teams. (low confidence) — https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3340764.3340771 · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] Personas represent fictional people but must draw their substantive characteristics from research about real users. Research-based behaviors, attitudes and goals are central; irrelevant biographical detail should not displace information that informs design decisions. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/persona/ · keywords: UI/UX design: research methods, UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/personas-jobs-be-done/
